trust_decision.summary: Whether embedded $type names in each App.txt settings line (from the app data dir, which a launch argument can redirect) are trusted to pick the .NET type that Newtonsoft instantiates; decided by the shared JsonSettings TypeNameHandling value used in ReadSettingsFile.

landing_point.why: Searching for TypeNameHandling turns up exactly one hit, the static JsonSettings in App.xaml.cs, and that is the whole published fix.

fix_sites.entry_point: App startup: ReadSettingsFile on App.txt from the AppData path or the path given as the first command-line argument (App.xaml.cs:20-55, 88-106)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No route is left to dismiss: the only other JSON deserialisations (ADB Explorer/ViewModels/Device/Devices.cs:87, ADB Explorer/Services/AppInfra/Network.cs:31) use Newtonsoft defaults with no type-name handling.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Saved-device history written by older versions (with type names embedded) must still load: Devices.RetrieveHistoryDevices detects the legacy format by finding the HistoryDevice type name in the raw string and picks the target type explicitly. Settings also round-trip through WriteSettings with the same JsonSettings. An over-broad fix, such as rejecting any line that contains $type or throwing away the settings file, would break legacy history and settings migration.

O6_input_shapes: single JSON value per settings line (object with $type)

O7_producer.where: ADB Explorer/App.xaml.cs:88-106 (ReadSettingsFile) with writer at ADB Explorer/App.xaml.cs:154

O8b_injection_room.sibling: History-device restore deserialising SavedDevices with its own settings object that keeps TypeNameHandling.Auto/Objects so polymorphic legacy device types still load
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The code already branches on a legacy type name (Devices.cs:84-85), so a maintainer wanting polymorphic HistoryDevice/StorageDevice lists could plausibly have added type-name handling here, in a separate file from App.xaml.cs.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A typed Retrieve<T> helper that re-deserialises a stored string through a JsonSerializerSettings with TypeNameHandling for complex settings values
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Storage is the generic settings accessor, and a helper that converts raw strings into typed objects is a natural addition.

O9_family: insecure deserialization (Newtonsoft TypeNameHandling on a local settings file)

O10_build.project_tests: ADB_Test/Tests.cs exists but has no settings/JSON/Storage tests

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Set TypeNameHandling.None on the shared JsonSettings (which is the published fix, and complete).

out_of_scope_notes: Clipboard/drag-drop formats (ADB Explorer/Services/AppInfra/CopyPasteService.cs:393-395) are parsed from raw MemoryStreams via custom struct readers, not a type-resolving deserializer; not pursued.
Network.cs:31 parses the GitHub releases response with default Newtonsoft settings (no type names); not part of this advisory.
unverified: needs_gpu_kernel_gui: Application_Startup is a WPF App method; the settings-parsing logic is a local function inside it and would need extraction to test headless. Flagged on that basis.
Exact advisory text was not available; the trust decision is inferred from the fix diff and the code.
Second fix commit f07050c only deletes a Dutch .resx translation and is unrelated to the vulnerability.
